user.title: Create a backdated sensor
user.description: Mirrors a numeric sensor and records each value at the time it was captured, for example when a car measured its battery level, instead of when Home Assistant received it.

data_description.source: Sensor whose numeric state is mirrored.

timestamp.title: Capture time
timestamp.description: Where does the time a value was captured come from? A time can be an ISO 8601 text or a Unix time in seconds or milliseconds. When it comes from another entity, the value and the time are paired once both have stayed unchanged for 5 seconds.

data_description.timestamp_attribute: Attribute holding the time the source sensor's value was captured.

data_description.timestamp_entity: Entity whose state is the capture time, such as a timestamp sensor.
Entity with an attribute holding the capture time. The attribute is chosen next.

data_description.timestamp_property: Last changed: when its state last changed. Last updated: when its state or an attribute last changed. Last reported: when it last reported, even without a change.

data_description.timestamp_template: Renders the capture time. The variable `source` holds the entity ID of the source sensor, and `now()` gives the time a change was received.

data_description.timestamp_delay: The capture time is the time a value was received, less this delay.

details.title: Unit and classes
details.description: The unit and the classes are taken from the source sensor and can be changed.

data_description.state_class: Long-term statistics are kept only with a state class. Hourly statistics compiled before a backdated value arrived are then recomputed.

error.unit_not_valid: The unit of measurement does not fit the device class.
error.state_class_not_valid: The state class does not fit the device class.
error.entity_is_source: The source sensor's state is the value itself. Choose another entity.
error.template_not_a_time: The template does not render a time.

init.title: Change the backdated sensor
init.description: After a change, the current value stays until a value captured later arrives.
